This example describes one imaginary electrical load. It is not a Faunapoolen package specification, a recommended operating schedule or a quoted electricity tariff. Assume a constant input of 100 watts, operation for 24 hours a day over 180 days, and a variable electricity cost of SEK 2.00 per kilowatt-hour excluding VAT.

  1. Convert power: 100 W ÷ 1,000 = 0.1 kW.
  2. Calculate operating time: 24 hours × 180 days = 4,320 hours.
  3. Calculate energy: 0.1 kW × 4,320 hours = 432 kWh.
  4. Calculate this load's cost: 432 kWh × SEK 2.00/kWh = SEK 864 for the stated period.

At an assumed SEK 3.00 per kilowatt-hour, the same 432 kWh would cost SEK 1,296. Both figures exclude VAT and cover only that load and period. Add every actual component and any operation outside the example period. Lighting, additional circulation or heating, if part of the design, need their own entries.

Replace the example price with the relevant variable charges from your supply and network agreements, excluding VAT consistently. Fixed charges and any demand-based network charge are outside this simple multiplication. Check your provider's billing model before attributing a change in the household bill to the pool.

For warmer water and a longer season, our nature pool heating guide explains what affects the heating budget.

Budget for water using volume

Keep the initial filling separate from later top-ups and water used during maintenance. Ask how volume will be estimated or recorded, then use the applicable local water tariff, including any wastewater charging that actually applies. If water must be delivered, obtain a separate delivery price rather than using the municipal rate.

Do not assign an automatic full refill to every year, or assume that no further water will be needed. Follow the system's care plan and investigate unexplained losses. Our permissions and water-planning guide explains why filling and disposal arrangements need local confirmation.

Include your time and the work you will buy

Decide which routine tasks you want to do and which you would prefer to arrange with a service provider. Ask for a description of a visit, its price and what is excluded. Travel, consumables or replacement parts may be separate; a service price is only comparable when the scope is clear.

List care materials and tests specified for the actual installation, without assuming every system uses the same products. Our seasonal care guide helps organize the work. Reducing required circulation or postponing necessary care is not a reliable cost-saving plan.

Leave room for replacement and review

Ask about warranties, serviceable parts and replacement options for the proposed equipment. A repair reserve is a budgeting choice, not a claim that every pump fails after a fixed number of years. Keep it separate from routine operating costs so the annual comparison stays understandable.

After the first season, review recorded energy, water, bought materials and service invoices against the assumptions. Use that evidence to improve the next year's budget. To start with the initial investment, compare our packages and ask for the ownership questions to be included in your proposal.

Calculation and source checked: 17 September 2026. All example inputs are hypothetical; no savings comparison or annual cost guarantee is implied.
translations.blog.varma-upp-naturpool.bodyHtml:
Can a nature pool be heated?

Yes, a nature pool can be heated when its filtration and equipment are designed for it. Biological water treatment does not automatically mean cold water. The important question is which temperature and swimming season your particular pool can support.

Perhaps you want a more inviting morning dip, or a few more weeks of swimming at either end of summer. Those are useful starting points for the design. Heating should be considered alongside the water volume, filtration, position in the garden and running budget.

Choose the swimming season you want

Start with when you will actually use the pool. Keeping water comfortable for summer afternoons is a different task from heating it through cool spring nights. A larger temperature difference between the water and its surroundings generally means more heat to replace.

Before choosing equipment, write down three things:

  • Your swimming months. Summer only, or a longer season into spring and autumn?
  • Your preferred water temperature. Bring a target to the discussion so we can assess it against the proposed system.
  • Your everyday routine. Daily swims, weekends or occasional visits to a holiday home?

These choices help make an energy estimate meaningful. A low running-cost figure tells you very little if it assumes a shorter season or cooler water than you want.

Keep heating and biological filtration working together

A nature pool relies on a living filtration system. Its operating conditions matter, so there is no single maximum temperature that applies to every design. The agreed temperature range must suit the filtration, circulation and installed equipment.

A heater also needs the correct water flow and connections. The pump that circulates water through the filter is not itself a pool heater. If you already have a nature pool, have the existing system assessed before adding heating or changing its operating settings.

Heating does not replace water checks or routine care. Keep following the care plan, including the required circulation, even when you are not swimming. Our guide to biological filtration explains what is happening around the swimming area.

Keep the warmth in the water

Evaporation carries heat away from an outdoor pool. An exposed position and wind across the water can increase those losses. Looking at shelter and the pool's position is therefore part of planning the heating, not just choosing a pleasant place to sit.

A suitable cover can reduce evaporation and heat loss when the pool is not in use. On a nature pool, its fit needs particular attention: irregular edges, planted areas and access to the water all affect what will work. Include storage and how easily you can put the cover on and take it off.

Choose a cover that suits the actual pool system. A thermal cover or leaf net is not automatically a safety cover; the safety arrangements need to be considered separately.

What does a heat pump do?

An air-source pool heat pump uses electricity to transfer heat from the outdoor air into the water. Its output and efficiency change with the conditions. A headline rating measured in warm air does not tell you how it will perform on a chilly April morning.

For a longer season, ask for performance information at the air and water temperatures you expect to use. Plan space for airflow, maintenance and condensate drainage, and consider the sound near seating areas and neighbouring gardens. Electrical supply and installation belong in the proposal too.

What will heating cost?

Keep the installed heating price separate from its running cost. The latter depends on the pool, weather, target temperature, cover use and length of the season. There is no useful annual figure without those assumptions.

For an electricity estimate, multiply the heating system's expected electricity consumption in kilowatt-hours by your applicable electricity price. Use electricity consumed, not the heat delivered to the water. Include heating separately from filtration, lighting and other equipment so the total is easy to understand.

Ask to compare two scenarios: the season you ideally want and a shorter season or lower temperature that you would still enjoy. Our guide to owning a nature pool shows how to organise the wider running budget.

Plan the end of the season too

A heated pool is not automatically a pool for year-round swimming. Pipes, pumps and the heater still need a winter plan suited to the installation. Agree when heating should stop, how the equipment is protected from frost and what is needed before restarting in spring.

If warmer water is part of your idea, mention it when you tell us about your pool. We can assess the possibilities with the design and make the scope clear in your proposal. Heating is assessed separately; do not assume it is included in a package starting price.
translations.blog.why-you-should-get-a-natural-pool.b:
A swimming place that belongs in the garden

A nature pool combines a swimming area with biological treatment. Stone, planting and the water's edge shape how it feels from the terrace or inside the house, as well as when you are in the water. It can be somewhere to spend time even on a day when you do not swim.

Start with the moments you want more of. Do you want a short dip before breakfast, room for swimming or a place where family and friends can sit nearby? These choices are more useful than choosing a pool by photograph alone.

Think beyond the summer swim

Consider the view in autumn, the route from the house and where you might sit in spring. A pool can remain part of the garden through the seasons, but that does not mean every installation can be used for swimming in every weather.

If cold bathing is part of your idea, discuss access and the system's winter operation from the start. Do not assume winter use or heating is included in a particular package.

The care that comes with it

Biological filtration changes the way water is treated; it does not remove the need for checks. Leaves and debris need collecting, plants need attention and circulation needs monitoring. At handover, we show the tasks for your system and provide a maintenance plan.

The guide to care through the year helps you think about these responsibilities before deciding. Consider who will look after the pool when you are away.

Space, budget and expectations

The advertised swimming area is not the entire footprint. Filtration, edges, paths and equipment access also need room. A site assessment connects those needs with the shape and ground conditions of your garden.

Starting prices help compare the scale of options; a quotation needs an agreed scope. Include the surroundings and ongoing care in your budget. Neither future savings nor an increase in property value should be assumed.

See a real pool on Gotland

Our completed nature pool on southern Gotland lets you see a Faunapoolen project and hear Brita's account. Use it to identify details you like, while remembering that its setting and layout are specific to that property.

For the broader choice between pool types, read the existing comparison of natural and conventional pools.

Choose around the way you want to swim

Our pool packages offer three starting points for a conversation about scale. They do not replace a design for your site. Compare the pool options and what is included, then tell us about the garden and the everyday moments you want to create.

translations.site.commercial.gardenGuideLink: Plan water features with your garden
translations.site.commercial.waterscapeArea: We design water features throughout Sweden and in Denmark. Tell us about your garden and we will discuss the right scope; ponds and streams are quoted individually.
translations.site.commercial.pricingTitle: What does a nature pool cost?
translations.site.commercial.pricingIntro: Choose a starting point for your garden. We’ll help you understand what your site needs and agree a clear scope before you decide.
translations.site.commercial.scopeTitle: What does your pool package cover?
translations.site.commercial.scopeBody: Every package includes design, project coordination, excavation in accessible ground without rock, the liner and filtration system, installation, stone edges and aquatic planting. Start-up, a personal handover and a first-season site visit are included too.
translations.site.commercial.scopeDetail: Rock excavation, groundwater work, restricted access, soil removal, electrical supply, filling and transport are priced for your site. We coordinate the work and itemise these costs in your quotation before you agree to construction.
translations.site.commercial.groundBody: We assess the ground, levels and access for machinery so your quotation reflects the work your garden needs.
translations.site.commercial.sizeBody: Your swimming area and filtration are planned together. The space you need and the way you want to swim guide the design.
translations.site.commercial.surroundingsBody: Stone edges and aquatic planting are included. Additional terraces, garden lighting and landscaping are agreed and priced separately in your quotation.
translations.site.commercial.footprintTitle: Swimming area is not the whole footprint
translations.site.commercial.footprintBody: Swimming area is the water you swim in. The approximate total footprints also include filtration and edges, based on each package’s starting size. Allow extra space for terraces and paths. We agree the full layout for your garden before construction.
translations.site.commercial.ownershipTitle: Budget for life with the pool
translations.site.commercial.ownershipBody: A nature pool needs routine care and electricity for circulation. Your system, operating time, water needs and choice of servicing affect running costs. We explain the tasks at handover and provide a maintenance plan; biological filtration does not mean no maintenance.
translations.site.commercial.pricingQuestionTitle: Do I need to choose a package before we talk?
translations.site.commercial.pricingQuestionBody: No. The packages help you compare scale and investment. You can enquire about one or leave the choice open. We start with your garden, the way you want to use it and your budget.
translations.site.commercial.waterPriceTitle: Prices for ponds, streams and fountains
translations.site.commercial.waterPriceBody: These are separate projects from the swimming-pool packages. We discuss the site, size, circulation and materials with you and provide an individual quotation.
translations.site.commercial.waterfallPriceBody: The length, levels and access for equipment affect the design. Tell us where you would like to hear and see the water; we work out the scope before quoting.
translations.site.commercial.fountainPriceBody: A fountain or small pond has its own requirements for water supply, circulation and installation. Ask us about your space; nature-pool starting prices do not apply to these installations.
translations.site.packageScope.betweenSizes: We also design pools between these sizes. Total footprints include filtration and edges.
translations.site.packageScope.included.title: Included in every pool
translations.site.packageScope.included.body: We design and coordinate your pool, including excavation in accessible ground without rock. The liner, filtration, pumps, pipework, installation, stone edges and aquatic planting are all included. We start the system with you, provide a personal handover and return for a site visit during your first swimming season.
translations.site.packageScope.site.title: Quoted separately
translations.site.packageScope.site.body: Rock excavation, groundwater work and restricted access are assessed and priced for your site, along with the removal and disposal of surplus soil. Electrical supply, water filling and transport are quoted separately, as are any decks, terraces or landscaping beyond the pool.
translations.site.packageScope.coordination: We coordinate excavation, deliveries and the electrician. Site-specific costs are itemised in your quotation and agreed with you before construction.
translations.site.comparison.title: Nature pool costs and care
translations.site.comparison.investmentBody: A nature pool typically costs more upfront than a comparable conventional pool, including its biological filtration and planted areas.
translations.site.comparison.runningBody: Biological filtration removes routine chlorine costs and can reduce operating costs compared with a conventional pool.
translations.site.comparison.careBody: Care focuses on removing leaves, checking circulation and tending plants. Allow additional time for seasonal maintenance.
translations.site.packages.glade.description: A compact plunge pool for cooling off, sauna breaks and smaller gardens.
translations.site.packages.summer.description: A pool for swimming together, with natural stone, lighting and water jets.
translations.site.packages.summer.includes.0: Wetland filtration and a separate water intake
translations.site.packages.horizon.description: A spacious pool with waterfalls, boulders and a planted landscape.
translations.site.copy.home.title: Make your garden the best part of being home.
translations.site.copy.home.ingress: As an Aquascape™ certified contractor, we design and build nature pools for morning swims, long summer evenings and time together.
translations.site.copy.home.caseBody: We built this nature pool beside Brita’s home on southern Gotland, with natural stone edges that connect it to the surrounding garden. Today, it’s a place for her and her grandchildren to swim and spend time together.
translations.site.copy.home.processTitle: From the first idea to your first swim.
translations.site.copy.home.waterscapeTitle: A place to pause in your own garden.
translations.site.copy.home.waterscapeBody: Watch the fish, listen to a stream or settle beside a quiet pond. From long summer evenings to crisp winter mornings, we create water features to enjoy throughout the year, outdoors or from the warmth of home.
translations.site.copy.naturePools.title: A natural place to swim. A lovely place to be.
translations.site.copy.naturePools.ingress: Clear water, natural stone and planting that belongs in your garden. We bring them together in a nature pool designed for you, from the first ideas to your first swim.
translations.site.copy.naturePools.careTitle: What care does a nature pool need?
translations.site.copy.naturePools.careBody: Biological filtration still needs routine care. At handover, we show you the tasks for your system and provide a maintenance plan.
translations.site.copy.naturePools.carePoints.0: Remove leaves and debris, and check water level and circulation.
translations.site.copy.naturePools.carePoints.1: Care for the plants and follow the seasonal plan for your system.
translations.site.copy.naturePools.carePoints.2: We also offer servicing, spring start-up and winter preparation.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.title: Your own place to slow down.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.ingress: A pond to spend time beside or a stream within earshot of the terrace. We design and build ponds, streams and waterfalls for your garden.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.typesTitle: What would you enjoy coming outside for?
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.types.0.title: Koi ponds
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.types.0.body: For time spent watching the fish. We plan depth, shelter and filtration for the pond, and explain the care it needs.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.types.1.title: Streams and waterfalls
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.types.1.body: For the sound of moving water near a favourite seat. We plan the flow, levels and access for maintenance.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.types.2.title: Fountains
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.types.2.body: For the gentle sound of water beside a terrace or favourite seat. We help you choose a fountain that suits your garden and the space you have.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.methodTitle: Designed for your garden. Planned for care.
translations.site.copy.waterscapes.methodBody: The right choice depends on your space, budget and how much care you want to take on. We plan circulation and filtration, with equipment you can reach for servicing.
translations.site.copy.guides.title: Ideas and guides
translations.site.copy.guides.ingress: Explore nature pools, ponds and water gardens, with practical advice on design, natural filtration and everyday care.
translations.site.copy.about.title: About Faunapoolen
translations.site.copy.about.ingress: We bring construction, business and design together to create nature pools and water gardens. Meet the people behind Faunapoolen.
translations.site.copy.about.methodTitle: You should not have to become a pool expert.
translations.site.copy.about.methodBody: We explain the choices and what affects the cost, then plan and build the solution for your property. At handover, we show you how to care for it.
translations.site.copy.about.companyTitle: A Swedish specialist in nature pools
translations.site.copy.about.companyBody: Faunapoolen is a Swedish company designing and building nature pools, ponds and water gardens. We bring water, natural stone and planting together so each project feels part of its surroundings. Our work extends beyond the pool itself, from the surrounding garden to ongoing care as it grows and changes.

translations.site.faq.title: Questions about nature pools
translations.site.faq.site.question: Could a nature pool work in my garden?
translations.site.faq.site.answer: We assess available space, access for construction, ground conditions and levels. You can start with a conversation about your garden before deciding on a design.
translations.site.faq.space.question: How much space does a nature pool need?
translations.site.faq.space.answer: The package areas describe swimming space. Filtration, pool edges and access need additional room, depending on the design. We assess the whole layout before proposing a size; the swimming area alone does not tell you whether a pool will fit.
translations.site.faq.price.question: What does a nature pool cost?
translations.site.faq.price.answer: Our pool options show indicative starting prices excluding VAT and shipping. Ground conditions, access, size and materials affect the quotation. Ponds, streams and other water features are quoted individually.
translations.site.faq.care.question: How do I care for a nature pool?
translations.site.faq.care.answer: Routine care includes removing leaves and debris, checking water level and circulation, and caring for plants. We explain the tasks for your system at handover. Servicing, cleaning and seasonal help are also available.
translations.site.faq.ready.question: Do I need a design before contacting you?
translations.site.faq.ready.answer: No. You do not need drawings or a chosen package. We start with how you want to use the garden, your ideas and your budget.
translations.site.faq.consultation.question: What does a consultation cost?
translations.site.faq.consultation.answer: The first phone consultation is free. The planning visit is paid and includes a site assessment and project discussion. Its fee is deducted from the installation cost if you go ahead. Your first-season follow-up visit after installation is included in the pool package.
translations.site.faq.next.question: What happens after the first call?
translations.site.faq.next.answer: We agree the next step with you. If a site visit is needed, we discuss that before moving on to a design proposal and quotation.
translations.site.faq.types.question: What can you build?
translations.site.faq.types.answer: We design and build nature pools, koi ponds, reflecting ponds, streams, waterfalls and fountains. We also work with water storage and help with existing installations.
translations.site.faq.filtration.question: How is the water filtered?
translations.site.faq.filtration.answer: Pumps circulate the water through mechanical and biological filtration. Filters catch debris, while microorganisms take up nutrients that can feed algae. We select and size the Aquascape™ system for the installation.
translations.site.faq.custom.question: Can I choose the shape and materials?
translations.site.faq.custom.answer: Yes. We develop the shape, edging and planting with you. Features such as waterfalls and lighting can be discussed as part of the design; the quotation confirms what is included.
translations.site.faq.garden.question: Can you include the surrounding garden?
translations.site.faq.garden.answer: Yes. We also build patios and retaining walls, lay paving and plan planting. We agree how much of the surrounding garden to include in your project and quotation.
translations.site.faq.winter.question: What happens to a nature pool in winter?
translations.site.faq.winter.answer: Winter care depends on the system and site. We explain whether your installation should keep running or be prepared for winter closing, and can help with the work.
translations.site.faq.mature.question: How does the installation change over time?
translations.site.faq.mature.answer: Plants grow and establish themselves, so pruning and plant care are part of the routine. The biological filtration also needs time to establish; we explain what to expect for your system.
translations.site.faq.location.question: Where do you build nature pools?
translations.site.faq.location.answer: We build nature pools throughout Sweden and in Denmark, including Skåne, Halland, Blekinge and Småland. Tell us your town or postcode so we can discuss the property and agree the next step.
translations.site.faq.existing.question: Can you help with an existing pond or pool?
translations.site.faq.existing.answer: Yes, including installations built by someone else. We offer cleaning, maintenance, repairs and upgrades such as filtration improvements and leak detection. Contact us to discuss an assessment.

translations.site.gotland.story.home.body: Just outside the house, the garden opens onto water. We built this nature pool to feel part of the surroundings, with room for a swim and a place to spend time together.
translations.site.gotland.story.stone.heading: Stone, water and a softer edge
translations.site.gotland.story.stone.body: Natural stone gives the pool its shape, while planting connects the water to the garden. The irregular edges make each view a little different as you move around the pool.
translations.site.gotland.story.garden.heading: Part of the garden, even between swims
translations.site.gotland.story.garden.body: A nature pool brings more to a garden than a place to swim. Reflections, ripples and planting give you something to enjoy from the water’s edge or from inside the house.

translations.site.poolLanding.reassurance: Your first phone consultation is free. No finished plan needed.
translations.site.poolLanding.questionsTitle: A few answers before we talk.
translations.site.poolLanding.benefitsIntro: You want a place to swim that feels at home in your garden, without the regular chemical treatment of a conventional pool. But it can be hard to know what will fit, what it will cost or where to begin. We help you find a design that suits your space, your budget and the way you want to enjoy the water.
translations.site.poolLanding.caseBody: A finished Faunapoolen project on southern Gotland, designed around the house and garden with natural stone edges and planting.
translations.site.poolLanding.certificationBody: Aquascape™ certified expertise, from planning and construction to showing you how to care for your pool.
translations.site.poolLanding.priceIntro: Explore three starting points, from a compact plunge pool to a larger pool for swimming. We’ll help you choose the size and features that suit you.
translations.site.poolLanding.scope: Your quotation confirms the full scope, including what is covered for excavation, soil removal, electrical work, filling and transport. We agree this with you before you commit.
translations.site.poolLanding.steps.0.title: Tell us about your garden
translations.site.poolLanding.steps.0.body: Start with a free phone conversation about your space, budget and ideas. No drawings or package choice needed.
translations.site.poolLanding.steps.1.title: Choose your design
translations.site.poolLanding.steps.1.body: After a site assessment, review your design and quotation. You decide what goes ahead before construction begins.
translations.site.poolLanding.steps.2.title: Enjoy your first swim
translations.site.poolLanding.steps.2.body: We build your pool, start the system and show you how to look after it, with a care plan to take with you.
translations.site.poolLanding.timing.question: How long will the build take?
translations.site.poolLanding.timing.answer: The schedule depends on the design, ground conditions and access. We discuss your preferred timing and agree a project schedule before work begins, so you know what to expect.
translations.site.poolLanding.disruption.question: What happens to the rest of my garden?
translations.site.poolLanding.disruption.answer: Building a pool involves excavation and access for machinery. We discuss which areas will be affected, where soil will go and what finishing work is included, so the agreed scope covers the garden as well as the pool.
translations.site.poolLanding.budget.question: What can change the final price?
translations.site.poolLanding.budget.answer: Ground conditions, access, filtration, materials and the surrounding garden all affect the cost. The starting prices exclude VAT and shipping; your quotation sets out the work and materials for your property before you decide.
translations.site.poolEnquiry.heading: Let’s find the right pool for your garden.
translations.site.poolEnquiry.body: Tell us where you’d like to build. In your free phone consultation, we’ll discuss what could fit, your budget and the next step.
translations.site.poolEnquiry.followUp: We’ll email you to arrange a time. If you’d prefer a call, leave your phone number.
translations.site.poolEnquiry.received: Thank you. We’ll get in touch to arrange your free pool consultation. There’s no commitment to a design or package.
translations.site.ownership.title: Life with your pool
translations.site.ownership.intro: A little care each week, with a clear plan for the seasons. Here is what to expect.
translations.site.ownership.body: Most routine care means clearing leaves, checking the water level and keeping circulation flowing. We show you these tasks at handover and provide a care plan for spring start-up, the swimming season and winter.
translations.site.ownership.care.title: How much care does it need?
translations.site.ownership.care.answer: Around 30 minutes a week in the swimming season.
translations.site.ownership.care.detail: Remove leaves, empty the skimmer and check the water level and circulation. Allow extra time for spring start-up, autumn leaves and winter preparation. Your care plan covers the equipment and planting in your pool.
translations.site.ownership.power.title: What does the electricity cost?
translations.site.ownership.power.answer: About SEK 230–460 a month for circulation, excluding VAT.
translations.site.ownership.power.detail: Calculated for 200–400 W of circulation running continuously for 30 days at SEK 1.60/kWh, excluding VAT. Your equipment and electricity tariff determine the cost. Heating, lighting, water and servicing are additional.
translations.site.ownership.build.title: How long does construction take?
translations.site.ownership.build.detail: This covers construction from excavation to handover. Planning and any permits come beforehand. Ground conditions, access, weather and the size of your pool affect the schedule, which we agree before work begins.
translations.site.aftercare.title: Confidence beyond the first swim.
translations.site.aftercare.guarantee.title: Your guarantees
translations.site.aftercare.guarantee.body: Your pool comes with a five-year guarantee on our installation work and three years on pumps and equipment. The pool liner is covered against manufacturing defects for 20 years.
translations.site.aftercare.handover.title: A personal handover
translations.site.aftercare.handover.body: We start the system together and practise the regular care tasks with you. You receive a care plan for your pool, covering the equipment, planting and each season.
translations.site.aftercare.followup.title: We come back
translations.site.aftercare.followup.body: At handover, we book your included first-season site visit. We check circulation, equipment and plant establishment, make the commissioning adjustments needed and answer your questions.
translations.site.aftercare.terms: Cover starts at handover. Workmanship covers installation defects; equipment and liner cover follow their product terms. Normal wear, frost damage and damage caused by missed care instructions are excluded. One first-season visit and commissioning adjustments are included; cleaning, routine servicing and later visits are quoted separately. Full terms accompany your quotation.
translations.site.poolDetails.filterTitle: A place to swim. A system working around it.
translations.site.poolDetails.filterBody: Your swimming area is part of a connected water system. Leaves are collected, water passes through biological filtration, and a pump keeps it moving. We plan these parts together, so you have room to swim while the filtration fits into the garden.
translations.site.poolDetails.filterCollectBody: A skimmer or intake area gathers floating debris where it can be removed, before it settles on the bottom.
translations.site.poolDetails.filterBioBody: Beneficial bacteria in the filter break down waste, while aquatic plants take up nutrients. The filter type and size depend on your pool.
translations.site.poolDetails.filterReturnBody: A pump circulates water through the system and back into the swimming area. We plan the flow and leave access for servicing.
translations.site.poolDetails.filterAlt: Architectural cutaway illustration of a natural swimming pool beside a planted gravel filter, showing the water, filter layers and a connecting pipe beneath the surface.
translations.site.poolDetails.fitTitle: Naturally part of your garden. Beautifully part of your day.
translations.site.poolDetails.fitBody: Start with how you want to use the water: a quick dip, swimming or time together. We then look at the whole garden, including filtration, the way into the pool and somewhere to sit. You do not need to work out the layout before we talk.
translations.site.poolDetails.fitSwimBody: The package sizes refer to the water you swim in. Shape, depth and steps are part of the design conversation.
translations.site.poolDetails.fitFilterBody: Filtration and equipment need space beyond the swimming area, with access for care and servicing.
translations.site.poolDetails.fitEdgeTitle: The way you use the garden
translations.site.poolDetails.fitEdgeBody: Stone edges, planting and a place to sit connect the pool to your home. We also assess ground levels and access for the build.
translations.site.poolDetails.fitAlt: Concept image: a nature pool with a planted edge and stone steps leading from a timber terrace into the water in a leafy garden.
translations.site.poolDetails.everydayTitle: A garden you spend more of your life in.
translations.site.poolDetails.everydayBody: You do not need a whole day free to enjoy the water. A nature pool brings swimming and time by the water into the garden you already call home.
translations.site.poolDetails.everydaySwimTitle: A swim whenever it suits you
translations.site.poolDetails.everydaySwimBody: Before breakfast or after work, step outside for a dip without packing a bag or driving to the beach.
translations.site.poolDetails.everydayTogetherBody: Bring your coffee to the water’s edge, read while someone swims, or stay outside a little longer when friends visit.
translations.site.poolDetails.everydayGardenTitle: Something to enjoy beyond the swim
translations.site.poolDetails.everydayGardenBody: Stone, planting and changing reflections give you something to enjoy from the terrace or the house, even on days you never get in.

translations.site.poolDetails.careTitle: Know what to do. Know who to ask.
translations.site.poolDetails.careBody: Before your first season, we walk you through your own system and give you a care plan. You will know what to check, how to look after the plants and when to arrange seasonal help.
translations.site.poolDetails.careRoutineBody: Remove leaves and debris, check the water level and flow, and follow the cleaning instructions for your equipment.
translations.site.poolDetails.careSeasonBody: Your plan covers plant care, spring start-up and winter preparation for your particular pool.
translations.site.poolDetails.careSupportBody: You can also arrange servicing, cleaning and seasonal help with us. We discuss the scope and cost separately.
translations.site.poolDetails.careAlt: Illustrative image: a fine-mesh net collecting fallen leaves beside the stone edge of a nature pool.
translations.site.poolDetails.careCaption: Everyday care starts at the water’s edge. Illustrative image.

translations.site.poolDetails.projectStoneBody: The close-up shows the stone beneath the water and the texture that continues along the pool’s edge.

translations.site.region.skane.title: A nature pool for your garden in Skåne
translations.site.region.skane.ingress: Make room for morning swims and more time outdoors. We design and build nature pools in Skåne, with the layout and biological filtration planned for your property.
translations.site.region.skane.focusTitle: Plan the pool and the places around it
translations.site.region.skane.focusBody: A pool can be one part of a larger garden project. Tell us whether you also want steps, a terrace or changes in level, so the design, budget and questions for your municipality cover the whole idea.
translations.site.region.skane.question1: Does the garden around the pool need permission?
translations.site.region.skane.answer1: Malmö’s guidance distinguishes the pool itself from other structures, such as a deck or pool house. Discuss the complete proposal with the municipality where your property is located before work begins.
translations.site.region.skane.question2: What if we also change the ground levels?
translations.site.region.skane.answer2: Malmö has separate guidance for retaining structures, decking and ground changes. Ask your own municipality which permissions apply to the proposed levels and construction, rather than assuming the pool decision covers everything.
translations.site.region.halland.title: A nature pool at home in Halland
translations.site.region.halland.ingress: A quiet dip before breakfast or an afternoon together by the water. We design and build private garden nature pools in Halland, around the way you want to spend time at home.
translations.site.region.halland.focusTitle: Plan water supply before the first swim
translations.site.region.halland.focusBody: Water filling is part of planning the installation. Tell us whether your property has municipal water or a private supply, so we can discuss the water needed and what to check with your supplier before starting.
translations.site.region.halland.question1: Can I fill the pool during a water restriction?
translations.site.region.halland.answer1: Laholmsbuktens VA says that pools must not be filled with municipal drinking water when a watering ban applies. Check the current rules with your water supplier before planning the fill.
translations.site.region.halland.question2: What should I check before building in Halmstad?
translations.site.region.halland.answer2: Halmstad’s building guidance includes pools, changes in ground level and safety around the water. Contact your municipality with the proposed layout so that any permissions and safety measures are considered before construction.
translations.site.region.blekinge.title: A nature pool for your garden in Blekinge
translations.site.region.blekinge.ingress: Bring the water closer to everyday life. We design and build nature pools in Blekinge, with space for swimming and places to sit, gather and enjoy the garden.
translations.site.region.blekinge.focusTitle: Start with the conditions on your property
translations.site.region.blekinge.focusBody: The right layout depends on more than swimming area. We discuss access, levels and the space around the pool. If the property is near water or in a protected setting, identify the relevant planning questions early.
translations.site.region.blekinge.question1: What should I check for a property near the coast?
translations.site.region.blekinge.answer1: Karlskrona asks applicants to investigate conditions including local plans, shoreline protection, rising sea levels and cultural heritage. Whether any of these affects your project depends on the property; ask the municipality about your proposed work.
translations.site.region.blekinge.question2: Does a pool decision cover walls and a pool roof?
translations.site.region.blekinge.answer2: Karlskrona’s pool guidance notes that the design and related structures can affect the need for permission. Include walls, decking and any roof when you discuss the proposal with your municipality.
translations.site.region.smaland.title: A nature pool for your garden in Småland
translations.site.region.smaland.ingress: Make your garden a place for everyday swims and time together. We design and build nature pools in Småland, with the pool, biological filtration and surroundings planned as one.
translations.site.region.smaland.focusTitle: Find out what is below ground as well as above it
translations.site.region.smaland.focusBody: A layout needs to allow for existing pipes, cables and access as well as the places you want to enjoy. Bring the location and any available site information to the first conversation; you do not need a finished design.
translations.site.region.smaland.question1: What should I check before excavating?
translations.site.region.smaland.answer1: Växjö’s pool guidance highlights checking for buried services where the pool is planned. It also distinguishes the pool from a possible retaining wall or roof. Raise these questions before settling the position and ground levels.
translations.site.region.smaland.question2: Can I use the same planning advice throughout Småland?
translations.site.region.smaland.answer2: Start with the municipality where your property is located. Local plans and the proposed work matter to the assessment. Växjö provides a plan map and application guidance; properties elsewhere need the equivalent information from their own municipality.
translations.site.region.shared.coverage: Our work also takes us beyond southern Sweden: we build nature pools throughout Sweden and in Denmark.
translations.site.region.shared.planningBody: The sources below are local starting points. Your municipality assesses what applies to your property and proposal; guidance for one place is not a decision for another.
translations.site.region.shared.nextTitle: From your idea to a considered proposal
translations.site.region.shared.nextBody: Tell us your town or postcode, how you want to use the garden and what you have in mind. In the first free phone conversation, we discuss the possibilities and next step. A site visit is agreed separately and is paid, with the fee credited against installation if you proceed.

translations.site.region.shared.packageBody: Our three nature pool options help you compare swimming areas and indicative starting prices, excluding VAT and shipping. The layout and quotation are developed for your property.

translations.site.region.shared.caseBody: On southern Gotland, we built a nature pool beside Brita’s home. See the finished pool and read Brita’s account of the build and swimming with her grandchildren.

translations.cookies.title: Cookies and website statistics
translations.cookies.choice: Allow or reject statistics. Your choice does not affect your access to the website or your ability to send an enquiry.
translations.cookies.introduction: Faunapoolen uses browser storage to remember your choices. Optional Google Analytics statistics require your permission.
translations.cookies.statistics: With your permission, we measure page visits, interest in pool packages and progress through the enquiry form, including successful enquiries. Events include the page address without query parameters, page title, language, landing page and a broad source category such as search or referral. They do not include your name, email, phone number, address or message.
translations.cookies.google: Google provides the analytics service and receives cookie identifiers and technical information such as your IP address and browser information when analytics is active. We do not enable advertising cookies or personalised advertising.
translations.cookies.storageTitle: What is stored and for how long
translations.cookies.analyticsCookies: _ga and _ga_E1BFSP43WZ: optional first-party cookies used by Google Analytics to distinguish browsers and sessions. They are configured to expire after 180 days, renewed during use. Statistics are shared with Google.
translations.cookies.consentStorage: fp-analytics-consent-v1: local storage containing only your allow or reject choice. It remains until you change it or clear this website's browser data. It is not sent to Google.
translations.cookies.visitStorage: fp-analytics-visit: optional session storage for your landing page and broad source category. Used only after acceptance, removed when you reject statistics or end the browser session.
translations.cookies.languageStorage: fp-language-choice and fp-language-dismissed entries: session storage remembering your language selection or dismissal of a language suggestion. Removed when the browser session ends and not shared with Google.
translations.cookies.withdrawal: Open cookie settings in the footer of any public page and select reject to withdraw consent. This stops future analytics events and removes this website's Google Analytics cookies and visit context. It does not undo statistics already sent. You can also clear saved choices through your browser.

translations.site.poolBenefits.heading: Your own swimming spot, naturally.
translations.site.poolBenefits.body: Step outside for a morning dip, bring everyone together for an afternoon swim, or unwind beside the water. Your nature pool becomes part of the garden, with natural stone and planting around your own swimming spot. We help you choose the size, shape and features that suit your space and the way you want to spend time outdoors.

translations.site.poolBenefits.chlorine.body: Enjoy water cleaned by filtration and circulation, without the regular chlorine dosing of a conventional pool.
translations.site.poolBenefits.biology.heading: Let nature help clean your water
translations.site.poolBenefits.biology.body: Beneficial bacteria filter waste while plants absorb nutrients, helping keep your swimming water in balance.
translations.site.poolBenefits.garden.heading: Make the pool part of your garden
translations.site.poolBenefits.garden.body: Natural stone, planting and a shape suited to your space make your pool feel part of the garden.
translations.site.poolBenefits.environment.heading: Reduce your pool’s environmental impact
translations.site.poolBenefits.environment.body: Efficient pumps and fewer water changes help save resources, while keeping chemical pool treatments out of your garden.
